entities.summary: Zacatecas is the principal city within the municipality in Mexico of the same name, and the capital of the state of Zacatecas. Located in north-central Mexico, the city had its start as a Spanish mining camp in the mid-16th century. Native Americans had already known about the area's rich deposits of silver and other minerals. Due to the wealth that the mines provided, Zacatecas quickly became one of the most important mining cities in New Spain. The area saw battles during the turbulent 19th century, but the next major event was the Battle of Zacatecas during the Mexican Revolution when Francisco Villa captured the town, an event still celebrated every anniversary.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Zacatecas played a significant role in the Mexican Revolution, with Francisco Villa's capture of the town in 1914 being a pivotal event. The city's mining industry also contributed to its importance as a major economic center in New Spain.
